title: Finite Instructions and Solenoidal Shear Flows
main_claim: Theorem 1.1. Given a one-tape machine M and an input w, an algorithm produces a smooth, solenoidal, mean-zero force f on T^3. With zero initial data, Navier–Stokes has the unique classical solution (U,0). After t=1, U is 1-periodic and depends on M only. The particle labelled a_*=(1/8,3/8,1/2) enters the strip {1/2<x<1} if and only if M halts on w.
coverage:
Checked the following in detail:
- **Lemma 2.1 (recorder).** Determinism of all 7 rows. Each destination control has a fixed incoming displacement. Predecessor reconstruction works on the full domain: the mark bit separates the two ways into R_r, and the P guard separates the two ways into L_q. The checkpoint induction uses r0>=2 so that h'<=n+1<frontier. The microstep count 2(g-h')+4 is right.
- **Lemma 3.1 (shears).** Recomputed the composition of the four shears to diag(lambda,1/lambda). Checked the 2h bound, including |(1/lambda-1)s|<=h, with convexity covering partially completed shears.
- **Theorem 3.2.** During each stage the particle feels only its own mask: source and target collars are disjoint, and the height cutoffs have disjoint supports with Z_i=1 near z_i. The path stays inside the rho plateau. Divergence, mean and self-advection all vanish for every W_j. Gronwall uniqueness holds.
- **Corollary 3.3 (observer bound).** Checked.
- **Section 4.**
  - Radix table: the linear parts are diag(B^-d,B^d), and the full image rectangles are correct.
  - Gaps: sources are separated by kappa/B. Targets are separated by kappa/B^2, using the fixed incoming displacement plus the fact that destination and written letter determine the predecessor.
  - Geometry: all centers lie in K, and K+[-2h,2h]^2 sits inside the chart (1/32,31/32).
  - Safety bound: x<=3/16+kappa<1/2 on branches that start and end at nonterminal controls. A terminal target can only appear on the last step before halting.
  - The loader path and the smooth join at t=1 are fine, and each original step takes at least 6 microsteps, so periods do not accumulate in finite time.

Section 5 (optional variants) was only skimmed. I spot-checked the endpoints of the alternative shear schedule.
sibling_notes: This uses the same recorder/radix/branch-map approach as the family-376 siblings (Scalar-Potentials, Prefix-Instructions, Eventually-Stationary). The paper is self-contained and imports nothing from those companion papers. What is new here is the 7-stage transverse shear realization, which has zero self-advection and therefore pressure zero.
